payload.content: Scope this to the dropped-delta bug only. Read the pi-ai SSE parser and the Anthropic provider adapter, form a hypothesis, confirm with a minimal repro, and propose the smallest fix. Do not refactor unrelated code or tour the library.

The draw_shape tool's final argument is getting dropped intermittently — the canvas element shows up with x/y but no label. It only happens on the Anthropic provider. Please find the root cause; I think pi-ai is losing the last tool_call_delta when the Anthropic stream ends.

summary.text: Symptom: last partial-JSON delta missing, Anthropic-only. Hypothesis to test: the Anthropic adapter emits content_block_stop / message_stop and the parser finalizes the tool call before flushing the buffered argumentsDelta. I'll read the SSE parser's flush path, then the Anthropic adapter's stop handling, then reproduce with a recorded stream.

payload.content: The parser itself looks correct: it accumulates partial_json into buffer.argumentsDelta and finalize() parses the whole buffer. So the parser is not where the delta is lost. That points the finger at WHEN the adapter calls onChunk vs finalize — if finalize fires before the last content_block_delta is processed, the tail is gone. summary.text: Now I can see it. finalize() runs on content_block_stop. The trailing comment says the last input_json_delta and content_block_stop usually share a flush, but if the SSE reader splits a frame (the final delta lands in a separate TCP read after a partial frame boundary), the sse() generator can yield content_block_stop before re-yielding the buffered tail of the last delta — so finalize() parses an argumentsDelta that is missing its final bytes. That is the dropped label. Anthropic-only because only its adapter finalizes on content_block_stop instead of waiting for a coalesced end. I should confirm with a repro that splits the frame at exactly that boundary.

payload.content: Root cause confirmed by the repro: the Anthropic adapter calls finalize() on content_block_stop, but when the SSE reader splits the final input_json_delta across a frame boundary, content_block_stop is yielded before the buffered tail of the last delta is flushed. finalize() then JSON.parses an argumentsDelta missing its last bytes — that's exactly the dropped 'label'. It's Anthropic-only because only that adapter finalizes on content_block_stop; the OpenAI adapter finalizes on its stop event after the tool buffer is fully drained.

summary.text: Minimal fix: defer finalize() until the tool buffer is known-complete. Two narrow options — (a) move finalize() from content_block_stop to message_stop, after which no more deltas can arrive; or (b) have the sse() reader hold content_block_stop until its preceding content block's deltas are fully drained. (a) is the smallest, lowest-risk change and matches the OpenAI adapter's ordering. I'll recommend (a) plus pinning the repro as a regression test, not a parser rewrite.

payload.content: Recommended minimal fix: in providers/anthropic.js, move the finalize(buffer) call off content_block_stop and onto message_stop (before emitting the stop event), so the tool buffer is only parsed once no further deltas can arrive — this mirrors the OpenAI adapter and needs no parser changes. Ship scripts/repro-split-delta.mjs as a regression test that splits the frame before the final delta. Eve's own route handler should still accumulate deltas and parse only on the final tool_call, which is the correct contract regardless. Handoff: this is an upstream pi-ai patch; Eve's copilot route is already delta-safe and needs no change once pi-ai is bumped.
